verdicts.why: Four of the six sentences (superior dancing not often seen, often moving wrong, always here so often, had often suspected) carry plain frequency, which the first gloss holds; the other two (often only carelessness, not often united) are the in-many-cases gloss listed second.

senses.why: Learner keeps both 'many times' and the short intervals, both examples are frequency uses of the headword, and often in this sense describes without judging.
'In many of the cases' says what the gloss says, and both examples are the generalising 'it is often X' use rather than repeated occurrence.

Learner keeps both alternatives of the gloss; the two made examples are frequency uses, which is the only reading of often this synset admits, and the overlap with the first sense is OEWN's, not the writer's.

verdicts.why: Three sentences are the fixed phrase 'in order to' and one is the verb, so only two carry a listed noun sense, one command (received orders) and one arrangement (chronological order); the sentences split and the command sense listed first is one of the split.

senses.why: Learner keeps the superior and the must-be-obeyed, the example is the housekeeper's orders from her master, and a command is described, not judged.
'Follows a plan you can follow and understand' is a plain rendering of logical or comprehensible arrangement, and 'chronological order' is exactly that sense.

'Arranged neatly and as things should be' renders regular or proper arrangement, and both made examples ('in perfect order', 'in working order') are this condition sense rather than the sequence sense.

verdicts.why: All six sentences are 'after a pause' in conversation, a stretch of time during which the talk stops, which the first gloss holds; the second gloss is a near-duplicate and nothing sits below a sense the sentences use.

senses.why: Learner is the gloss in plain words, both examples are a pause of some minutes or a short pause in talk, and the word describes without judging.

'A short time in which nothing is being done' is a fair plain rendering of temporary inactivity; the two examples are indistinguishable from the first sense's, but so are the two OEWN glosses, so no wrong-sense fault is chargeable.

verdicts.why: Every sentence (principal people in the room, variety of people, people who suffer, other people, some people, different people) is human beings collectively, which is the first gloss.

senses.why: Learner keeps the men-or-women-or-children and the collectively, both book examples are this sense, and the word describes without judging.
'All the citizens of a country or a state, taken together' is the gloss, and the made example (the people of that country chose a new ruler) is the citizenry sense.

verdicts.why: Four sentences are coming to realise something (perceive her regard, perceived that she must wait, perceive that his partiality, never perceived that Lydia), the become-conscious-of gloss listed first; only 'on perceiving whom' and the tan are sensory.

senses.why: 'Come to be aware of something' is become conscious of in plain words, both examples are mental realisations, and the word describes without judging.
'By seeing, hearing, or feeling it' is an illustrative rendering of 'through the senses', and both made examples (a light far off, a faint smell of smoke) are sensory uses.

verdicts.why: All three sentences (probability of each statement, probability of error, a probability of gaining such a clue) are likelihood as a quality, the first gloss; none is a numeric ratio.

senses.why: Learner keeps all three parts of the gloss (the quality, a probable event, the most probable event), both examples are from the book in this sense, and the word describes without judging.

senses.why: Learner keeps move ahead and onward through space or time, both examples are walking onward, and the word describes without judging.

verdicts.why: Only one sense is listed and all six sentences (grave propriety, sacrifice to propriety, propriety of his friend's inclination, appeared with propriety, propriety of behaviour, complete propriety) are correctness or fitness of conduct.

senses.why: 'Behaviour that is correct, or that suits the occasion' keeps both correct and appropriate, both examples are the headword in this sense, and the candidate is right because to call conduct proper is to approve it against a standard, which a learner needs to know.

verdicts.why: Four sentences are solemn affirmation with a that-clause (protested that he never read novels, protested he must be mistaken, Mrs. Philips protested that they would have a game, he protested that she should receive no mark), the first gloss; 'protesting against his proposals' and the boy's objection are the opposition senses listed below.

senses.why: 'State seriously and firmly that something is true' is affirm or avow solemnly in plain words, both examples are declarations not objections, and the word in this sense describes without judging.
Learner keeps both action and words, 'protesting against his proposals' is expressing opposition, and the verb names the act without judging it.
'Say words that show you object to something' is utter words of protest, and the boy's 'protested that she should not' in an argument that ended only with the visit is a spoken objection.

verdicts.why: Three sentences are attributes a person has or lacks (not one agreeable quality, display of these qualities, the popular qualities), the first gloss, and three from the preface are the characteristic nature of the work (cosmic quality, Swiftian quality, subdivisions of quality), the third; the sentences genuinely split and the first sense is one of the split.

senses.why: 'A feature that belongs to a person or thing and marks it off from others' renders essential and distinguishing attribute, both examples are attributes of persons, and the word describes without judging.
'How good or how valuable something is' is a degree of excellence or worth, and 'the quality of the cloth was poor' is the grade sense; the word names a scale rather than judging.
'A feature that gives something the particular nature it seems to have' keeps the apparent individual nature of the gloss, and the cosmic and Swiftian qualities of the novel are that sense.
